::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Traces to the Nantong Transistor Factory, a 1966-founded state enterprise; largest shareholder is the state-linked Nantong Huada Microelectronics Group (19.91%) with the Big Fund holding 11.26%. In 2016, Tongfu and the Big Fund jointly paid $371 million for 85% stakes in AMD's Suzhou and Penang assembly and test facilities — a rare case of a Chinese OSAT firm acquiring a Western chipmaker's own packaging plants outright.
:::

**Chinese name:** 通富微电 (Tōngfù Wēidiàn)

## What does this facility make?

Chip assembly, test, and advanced packaging — including hybrid-bonding-based chiplet packaging and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) packaging, positioning it alongside JCET in China's advanced-packaging push.

## Why does it matter?

One of two mainland Chinese firms in the world's top five OSAT companies by revenue (JCET is the other) — reporting describes Tongfu as one of three Chinese firms that have begun HBM packaging, a capability central to AI-accelerator supply chains.
